title: Prompt Quality Workbench
description: Learners toggle the six clauses of a MicroSim generation prompt (skill, specification, version pin, output files, layout, tie-breaking rule) and see which decisions each omission hands to the model and which Chapter 5 failure modes it makes more likely, weighted by the difficulty of the request.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Prompt Design
AI-Assisted Code Generation
MicroSim Generation
Instructional Technology
publisher: MicroSims 2.0: Generating, Instrumenting and Evaluating Interactive Learning Objects with AI

learningObjectives: The learner will critique a prompt by identifying which decisions it leaves to the model and which failure modes those open decisions make more likely.

controls.label: Scenario
options: Hard: projectile lab with a live chart

controls.label: Reset
controls.action: Restore the starting prompt (skill, specification and layout clauses on)

userInterface.hover: Hovering a clause card shows an example of the clause; clicking a card toggles it.

variables: per-scenario risk level for each decision
assumptions: Each clause removes exactly one decision from the model
Links from decisions to failure modes are a teaching heuristic, not measured probabilities

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Critique by manipulation: remove a clause and observe which decisions and risks open up
keyQuestions: Which decision does this prompt leave to the model?
Which failure mode would you test for first, and why?
Why does a missing clause matter more for a harder request?
commonMisconceptions: A longer prompt is always a better prompt
An open decision guarantees the linked failure
The specification block alone makes the other clauses unnecessary
assessmentOpportunities: Name the open decisions in a given prompt and their linked failure modes
Justify which clause to add first for a given request
